A1.justification: Both PDFs describe ViTaPEs and contain complete, readable 20-page documents. Inspection of the text, equations, tables, figures, and appendices supports reliable matching despite substantial revisions and relocation.

before.justification: V1 reports original material recognition, object identification, cross-dataset transfer, and grasp prediction results, together with ablations and robustness experiments.

after.justification: V2 retains these empirical evaluations and adds projection-head ablations and additional baseline comparisons in Tables 2, 3, and 5.

M1.justification: V1 already specifies local positional encodings followed by a nonlinear projection, global positional encoding, and joint self-attention. Its Appendix D gives the same D-to-768-to-D LeakyReLU projection retained in v2. V2 clarifies tensor shapes, token-wise application, and CLS handling without establishing a changed implemented method.

E1.justification: Both versions use TAG, OF-Real, YCB-Slide, and Grasp, retaining material classification, object identification, transfer, grasp prediction, and tactile-masking scenarios. Renaming 'object detection' to 'object identification' clarifies the existing classification task; it does not introduce different task requirements.

E2.justification: V2 adds SigLIP2 to the cross-dataset comparison in Table 2. Table 3 additionally evaluates UniTouch and SigLIP2 for linear and zero-shot grasp prediction; UniTouch previously appeared only in the cross-dataset comparison. Existing comparators remain.

E3.justification: New Table 5 introduces controlled projection-head comparisons under identical protocols and compute budgets, including a parameter-matched linearized control. The added SigLIP2 baseline uses source-dataset SSL adaptation with a learning rate of 10^-5. Retained dataset splits, metrics, and principal training configurations remain unchanged.

E4.justification: V2 adds a central mechanism study comparing PE-after-g, Linearized-g, and No-g on TAG accuracy and OF-Real transfer (Table 5). It removes v1 Appendix A's positional-row uniqueness and projection-rank validation analyses. Existing positional-encoding, modality, masking, augmentation, and scaling studies are retained, with masking moved into the main text.

E5.justification: V2 newly specifies five-seed means for the main results in Table 1 and the positional-encoding ablations in Table 4, and uses this reporting for new Table 5. V1 already specified five seeds for masking experiments. No increase in existing run counts or addition of confidence intervals or significance tests is established.

E6.justification: New Table 5 reports OF-Real zero-shot accuracies of 45.7%, 51.4%, and 48.1% for the three controls versus 65.2% for ViTaPEs; Tables 2–3 add baseline results. Retained values also change: SSL TAG accuracy from 75.0% to 75.9%, 20%-masking accuracy from 75.0% to 75.2%, and Extended-model accuracy from 78.9% to 79.0%. V1's assumption-validation results are removed. Existing transfer and grasping scores are otherwise retained.

T1.justification: V1's injectivity, translation-equivariance, and entropy-preservation results, assumptions, and proofs in Section 3.4 and Appendices A–B are removed. V2 introduces Proposition B.1, requiring consistent permutation of tokens and global positional rows. It also corrects the attention decomposition to use blocks of the jointly normalized softmax matrix, explicitly retaining their coupling.

C1.justification: The abstract, introduction, and conclusion withdraw the prominent claims of provable injectivity, rigid-motion equivariance, and information preservation. V2 instead emphasizes explicit two-stage positional injection, controlled ablations, and narrowly scoped re-indexing consistency. The central empirical claims about recognition, transfer, and grasp prediction remain.

C2.justification: V2 reframes alignment as learning a shared positional vocabulary without assuming geometric calibration, replacing interpretations grounded in broad formal guarantees. It adds an explanation of positional conditioning across the nonlinear stem, interprets the parameter-matched ablation, and explains supervised-versus-SSL accuracy through end-to-end training versus frozen-encoder linear probing. The stated sensor, scaling, and data limitations largely remain.

D1.justification: V2 adds a dedicated tensor-shape and CLS specification, explicitly states that augmentations are applied independently across modalities, and clarifies classifier and checkpoint usage. It also documents SigLIP2 adaptation and preprocessing. These are additional reproducibility details; most existing hyperparameters, hardware, training costs, and project-page information are retained.

R1.justification: The related-work survey remains largely intact. V2 adds Banerjee et al., Diamond and Toso, and SigLIP2, while removing the theory references to Cover and Thomas and Puthawala et al. It also withdraws the positioning claim that ViTaPEs is the first visuotactile model supported by the stated theoretical guarantees.

P1.justification: The abstract, introduction, method explanation, transfer discussion, and conclusion undergo substantial rewriting around positional-injection stages. 'Multi-scale' becomes 'multi-stage,' and 'object detection' becomes 'object identification.' The theoretical section is removed, and the appendices are substantially condensed and reorganized around implementation and scoped consistency.

P2.justification: V2 changes typography, page geometry, and title/author layout throughout. Figure 1 replaces its texture axis with cross-sensor generalization, Figure 2 moves into the introduction, and Tables 2–3 become stacked instead of side by side. Table 4 gains a full-model reference column, Table 5 is new, and masking moves into the main text. V1's assumption-validation Figures 4–5 are removed.

improvement.justification: V1's central guarantees relied on a translation argument that did not transform learned positional tables consistently (Appendix B.2). V2 replaces this with an explicitly scoped joint re-indexing proof and adds controlled experiments testing the claimed mechanism (Table 5). Although the theoretical scope shrinks and its old diagnostics disappear, this resolves an important mismatch between claims and justification. Clearer implementation specifications, additional baselines, and expanded seed reporting further strengthen the paper.
